chunk: 2 of 2 — UNSEAL, CROSS-TABULATE, SCORE, FILE THE VERDICT. Chunk 2 judged nothing and built no pack.
supersedes: The chunk 1 handoff. Its next_step has been executed in full; nothing in it remains outstanding.
headline: Protocol A ran, and ours lost 5 of 5 — four at CONFIDENCE: high. The 4:1 in the answers is the SAME 4:1 as in the sealed key, not independent of it: on the one pair where ours sat on letter A the judge answered B, so deterministic positional bias is ruled out and the pairs do not need re-running with sides swapped. FIDELITY capped at 5, which is below 6, which blocks the wave. Verdict at corpus/90-verdicts/wave1/W1-VISUAL-BLIND-PROTOCOL-A-r1.{json,md}, schema-valid (node tools/verdict-validate.mjs, exit 0). This is the first blind fidelity comparison in the project's history.
what_i_could_not_do: I DID NOT JUDGE AND COULD NOT HAVE. Rule 25 and RI-VIS06 §A. The five answers were collected before I started; my job began at the sealed key. If the judging was wrong, nothing in this verdict detects it — I am reading returns, not images. I also did not re-judge, re-run or seek a second opinion on any pair: ours won nothing, so §C's escalation ladder does not fire, and re-running a loss 'to check' is judge-shopping which the item forbids by name.

I COULD NOT PROVE THE KEY WAS UNREAD BEFORE JUDGING — ONLY SHOW WHEN IT WAS FIRST READ. The mount is `relatime`, so an atime records the FIRST read after a write and is not refreshed by later reads inside 24h. Absence of a late atime is therefore not evidence of absence of a read. What I can show: key files written 16:02:11–16:02:45Z, judgements captured 16:18:03Z, key opened by me after that.

AND I FOUND ONE READ I HAD TO CHASE RATHER THAN SKIP. `pairing.json` and `leakcheck.json` both name which arm is the reference and both were first read at 16:08:11.134Z — ten minutes BEFORE the judgements landed. It falls inside chunk 1's own run window (last artefact write 16:07:54Z, handoff status file 16:10:26Z), both files are quoted in chunk 1's handoff, and image-leakcheck.mjs reads `<pair>.reveal/mapping.json` and neither of these two, so it was not the tool. The consistent explanation is chunk 1 reading its own key while composing its own handoff — chunk 1 built the key, already knew it, and did not judge. That is not a violation. The alternative (the orchestrator reading it pre-dispatch) is NOT excluded by the timestamps alone, and I record that rather than asserting it away. It would not change the result either way: all five pairs were dispatched, one judge each, nothing withheld, and each judge received two file paths and the prompt text — key knowledge held by a dispatcher cannot reach a context that was handed two images.

THE POSITIONAL-BIAS CHECK HAS EXACTLY ONE DISCRIMINATING TRIAL. Chunk 1's free coin flips put ours on B in four of five pairs, so only pair03 can separate 'the judge answers A' from 'the judge answers the reference'. It separated, and the right way. But a design that rests its bias check on n=1 is a weak design and I say so rather than dressing the result up. Ruled reversibly below.

I COULD NOT REMOVE THE LARGEST DEVIATION, ONLY CHARACTERISE IT. The judges inherited the project CLAUDE.md and so were not naive about an in-development game existing; a subagent cannot be spawned without it in this harness. Direction of the residual bias is the part that matters and it is recorded: charity toward whatever looks like a game build flatters OUR side, so a losing verdict is STRENGTHENED by it. Owed remedy named; not mine to apply retroactively.
FOUR OF FIVE REFERENCE PLATES ARE FROM ONE GAME, THREE OF THOSE FROM ONE SESSION. Forced by pixel-density parity and not fixable inside this run. It narrows what 'modern reference' means here.
findings: THE CROSS-TABULATION, WHICH IS THE WHOLE JOB. pair01 A=ref B=ours, judge said A. pair02 A=ref B=ours, judge said A. pair03 A=OURS B=ref, judge said B. pair04 A=ref B=ours, judge said A. pair05 A=ref B=ours, judge said A. The answer letter tracks the SIDE on 5/5 and the POSITION on 4/5. A judge choosing by letter would have said A on pair03; it said B. Deterministic positional bias is ruled out outright, so no re-run with swapped sides is required. Honest limit: one informative trial, and under the null that answers are content-independent P(all five match the key) = 1/32 = 0.0313 — the same weak-power figure image-leakcheck prints about its own sweeps, quoted in the same spirit as a floor rather than a proof. Note which direction it runs: this statistic FAILS a build here, it does not pass one.

ONE FINDING REPEATED FIVE TIMES, NOT FIVE FINDINGS. Cluster A (no material response separation, flat untextured fills, no normal/roughness relief) — 4/5 pairs, named SINGLE BIGGEST GAP in 3 of them, all three at high confidence. Cluster B (no contact shadow, no ambient occlusion, forms floating on an unmodulated plane) — 5/5 pairs, the most universal observation in the set, biggest in 1. Cluster C (shadows crushed to near-black with no bounced or ambient fill) — 3/5. Those three are three faces of one condition: SURFACES IN OUR BUILD ARE NOT SHADED, THEY ARE FILLED. Cluster D (nothing above the ground plane) is genuinely separate — 1/5, medium confidence, on a bare-ground crop — and is the thinnest result here.

THE MECHANICAL STATISTICS AGREE WITHOUT BEING ASKED, AND ARE NOT ALLOWED TO ADD CONFIDENCE. image-leakcheck computed twelve statistics over the pack BEFORE anyone judged and reports the quality ones without gating on them; shadow_levels 5/5 and local_contrast_med 5/5 name the reference on every pair. That is cluster C and cluster A measured by an instrument with no opinion, on the same bytes. Recorded as corroboration of a forced choice already made — Ruling W2, and the standing instruction not to bolt a statistic onto a forced choice to firm it up.

WHAT OURS DOES BETTER, AND WHY IT DOES NOT PRODUCE A DRAW. All five 'WHAT THE LOSER DOES BETTER' lines name clean, stable, non-aliased silhouette edges on our side. Three of them describe blur or softness on the WINNING reference, which is partly chunk 1's declared bokeh confound on pair02/pair03 and partly the plates' own DOF and temporal blur. Ties are forbidden by the prompt and are not reintroduced through the back door here: sharp edges on an untextured, unshadowed surface are the absence of the defect, not the presence of a quality. Recorded as context.

THE RANKED, BUILDABLE REMEDY LIST — the deliverable the rest of the project consumes, at W1-VISUAL-BLIND-PROTOCOL-A-r1.md §3 with acceptance criteria per entry. R1 bind a real PBR material set (albedo + normal + roughness/metalness) to terrain, architecture and foliage — 4/5 pairs, biggest in 3, all high; this is the wave's named biggest visual gap, filed as GAP-W1-pbr-material-set-unbound so the gap ledger picks it up. R2 contact shadows + an AO term, and make all scene geometry cast into the shadow map — 5/5 pairs, the most universal single observation, biggest in 1. R3 an ambient/GI fill with tone-mapped shadow lift so shadows keep readable detail — 3/5, and one judge wrote the remedy itself. R4 dress the ground plane with props that cast and receive light — 1/5 at medium, ranked fourth and flagged as thin. R5 DEPTH OF FIELD IS LISTED TO BE STRUCK, NOT BUILT: its only support is pair02's second gap, and pair02's reference window IS background bokeh, so the confound manufactured it — pair04 and pair05 point the other way and credit ours with haze the reference window lacked.

SCORING RULING, REVERSIBLE. The spread is four `high` and one `medium`, which sits between rows 1 and 2 of RI-VIS06's outcome table. Row 2 (cap 7) states its own threshold as >= 2 at medium/low; one is not two, so row 2 does not apply and row 1 (cap 5) is the only remaining row describing a clean sweep of losses. No threshold was invented — the '>= 2' is doing exactly that work. Overturned by an amendment interpolating the cap across the spread, or by a re-run in which pair04's bare-ground window returns `high` in either direction. Recorded as a footnote in RI-VIS06 itself, marked as changing no number.

RULING S55'S ARITHMETIC, WHICH THIS IS THE FIRST RUN ABLE TO STATE AGAINST REAL PAIRS. Five pairs ran, so the zero-runs clause does not fire and BOTH its numbers are inert here. The counterfactual is the point: had this run not happened — the state of every wave before today — FIDELITY would have been capped at 7 under the pre-S55 text, landing EXACTLY on the wave-1 gate of >= 7.0 and costing nothing, versus capped at 2 with status FAIL under the amended text. What actually applies is the outcome table: cap 5. So running the backstop did NOT rescue the wave. It replaced an unearned pass (old text) or an unmeasured hard fail (new text) with a MEASURED 5 — still below 6, so RI-VIS06's own failure threshold blocks the wave via the RI-VIS01 §E min() gate, and below 7.0, so it does not meet the wave-1 bar either. What was bought is a blocked wave that knows exactly why, plus four remedies.

NONE OF RI-VIS06'S FIVE VOID CONDITIONS FIRED. Both protocols were not run by one agent (Protocol B has not been run at all). The key was not readable to any judge. The prompt was quoted byte-for-byte and not paraphrased. No run was discarded, so no discard needed a reason. No best-of-N: five judges, five pairs, zero re-asks. All five returned the required answer block on the first attempt and none mentioned the setting, so the prompt-leak discard condition did not trigger either.

FIVE PROTOCOL DEVIATIONS ARE IN THE VERDICT'S OWN method_deviations[] AND IN ITS §4, NOT IN A FOOTNOTE. D1 judges inherited CLAUDE.md (bias direction: flatters us, so it strengthens a losing verdict). D2 four of five plates from one game, forced by pixel-density parity (direction: unknown; a limit on generalisation). D3 pair02/pair03 reference windows are background bokeh (direction: against the reference — and ours lost both anyway, which makes those losses harder; its one real cost is that it manufactured the DOF 'gap'). D4 pair05 subject-scale mismatch (direction: against ours). D5 two reference windows moved after looking, to comply with §A's subject-neutral requirement (recorded by chunk 1 rather than applied quietly).

INSTRUMENT DEFECT RULED, REVERSIBLE. Wave 2's Protocol A must COUNTERBALANCE the side assignment — ours on A for exactly ceil(n/2) pairs, fixed before any image is looked at — rather than free-flipping it. A free flip can legitimately produce 5:0, under which the positional-bias check has NO power at all and the run is unfalsifiable on that axis. This is a blocked design decided in advance, not an adjustment made after seeing answers, and the letter carries no information a judge could use. Overturned if a judge could infer the balancing rule from the pack (it cannot — the rule lives in the runner and a judge sees two files), or if counterbalancing measurably changes the answers, which would itself be the finding.

RI-VIS06 AMENDED TWICE, SURGICALLY, BOTH INVITED BY THE ITEM. (1) Its Provenance note said 'Untested. No blind run has been executed at authoring time' and instructed the first wave to record format compliance; that sentence is now false for Protocol A, so it records the first execution and that all five judges held the required format on the first attempt with zero re-asks and zero discards — and states explicitly that NO amendment to the prompt text is made, because the predicted failure did not occur. Protocol B is still marked untested. (2) A footnote under the Protocol A outcome table recording how a four-high/one-medium spread reads. NO THRESHOLD WAS CHANGED and no number in the item was edited. Ownership checked before writing: no other live piece claims corpus/70-visual/RI-VIS06-blind-comparison-protocol.md.

EVIDENCE IS UNDER corpus/, NOT reports/, AND VERIFIED AGAINST THE REMOTE. HAZARDS §9: land.mjs builds a temporary index and runs `git add -A`, which honours .gitignore, so cited artefacts under reports/ can evaporate between staging and landing with nothing going red. All 24 cited paths — the ten pack images, the six key files, the five judgements/prompt files, both leak-check outputs and the verdict prose — were copied to corpus/90-verdicts/wave1/artifacts/W1-VISUAL-BLIND-PROTOCOL-A-r1/ and checked against the remote blob rather than against git status.

result.positional_bias: RULED OUT (deterministic). Answers track the key 5/5; the single pair with ours on letter A had its answer flip to B. No re-run with swapped sides required. Weak power: one discriminating trial, p=0.0313 under the content-independent null.
result.escalation_reason: RI-VIS06 §C fires only if ours wins a pair. Ours won none.
result.cap_row: Protocol A outcome table row 1 — ours loses all pairs at CONFIDENCE: high (row 2's >= 2 medium/low threshold is unmet at 1)
result.s55_zero_runs_clause: did not fire — five pairs ran
result.s55_counterfactual: had zero pairs run: cap 7 under the pre-S55 text (exactly the wave-1 gate of >= 7.0, costing nothing) vs cap 2 and status FAIL under the amended text
result.wave_effect: cap 5 < 6, so RI-VIS06's own failure threshold blocks the wave via the RI-VIS01 §E min() gate

next_step: NOTHING IS OUTSTANDING ON THIS TASK. Protocol A wave 1 is complete, filed and schema-valid. Four things are owed by whoever runs it next, and none of them is a re-judge of these five pairs: (1) counterbalance the side assignment, ours on A for ceil(n/2) pairs, fixed before looking; (2) run the judges from a working directory with no project CLAUDE.md in scope and record that the context was clean; (3) rebuild pair02/pair03 against one 1920x1080 in-focus daylight exterior plate — the pairing table is a one-line edit from doing it — and either acquire a low-light mid-distance exterior plate for pair05 or drop that pair and record the skip, which §E permits; (4) acquire 1920x1080 native plates across at least three more titles and two more lighting profiles, so 'modern reference' stops meaning 'Elden Ring'. Separately and more importantly: Protocol B has never been run at all, and RI-VIS06's side declaration forbids the agent that ran A from running it. And the actual work — R1 through R4 — belongs to the graphics builders, with wave 2's Protocol A as the test of whether it moved a judge that cannot see the label.

verification.leakcheck_rerun_after_reveal: node tools/blind/image-leakcheck.mjs --packs reports/blind/protocol-a-w1/PACK/packs --reveals reports/blind/protocol-a-w1-SEALED-KEY — GATE: GREEN, exit 0, identical verdict to chunk 1's pre-judging run. Its own weak-power caveat is quoted in the verdict rather than suppressed.
verification.ownership: node tools/ownership.mjs --conflicts and a scan of every status file's files_touched/files_claimed — no other live piece claims RI-VIS06 or the verdict paths.

cost.chunk_2: No GPU, no browser, no judge agents. Chunk 2 is filesystem reads, one leak-check re-run and the writing.
cost.chunk_1_carried_forward: two Pods (~$0.04 total), both confirmed terminated by API lookup.
